newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds mixed, tax collection helps.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds mixed, tax collection helps.

text.p: Argentina bonds were mixed late morning Wednesday with Brady bonds higher and local instruments down.
Traders said overall the market remained well supported, however, with the figures for May tax revenue released late Tuesday underlining the improving fundamentals of the market.
"The news of the tax collection was very good," said an analyst.
Tax revenue came in at $4.6 billion, up 28.6 percent on May 1996 and 17.3 percent higher than in April this year. The figure was the highest since 1991.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was up 1/4 at 93-1/4 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 4 due 2002 was down $0.15 at 116.65.
The analyst added that the tax collection bode well for the market because it meant Argentina was now likely to meet the second quarter deficit target agreed with the IMF.
"Bonds are reflecting that," said a trader.
